title: Conversations 1: Greetings and wishes
subtitle: Hello, Goodnight, Good luck!
summary: Greet people at any time of day, say goodbye and thank you, and use the right wish for birthdays, exams and special days.

lesson.heading: Hello and goodbye
lesson.text: Say **Hello** or, more informally, **Hi**. Before 12 o'clock say **Good morning**, in the afternoon **Good afternoon**, and after about 6 o'clock **Good evening**. When you leave, say **Goodbye**.

examples.note: See you soon is quite informal

lesson.heading: How are you?
lesson.text: **How are you?** is the usual question when you meet someone. Answer with **Fine, thanks. And you?** or **Not too bad, thanks.**

examples.text: *A:* How are you? *B:* **Not too bad, thanks.**

lesson.heading: Goodnight
lesson.text: When someone goes to bed, say **Goodnight**, and sometimes also **Sleep well**. Use Goodnight only when you or the other person leaves - never when you arrive.

examples.text: A child goes to bed. You say: **Goodnight. Sleep well.**
You leave a party at midnight. You say: **Goodnight!**

lesson.heading: Please, thank you and sorry
lesson.text: When you ask for something, say **Please**. When someone does something nice for you, say **Thank you** or, informally, **Cheers**. Say **Excuse me** to get past someone, **Sorry** when you do something wrong, and **Bless you** when someone sneezes.

examples.text: Some people are in the doorway. You say: **Excuse me!**
You stand on someone's foot. You say: **Sorry!**

lesson.heading: Special days and wishes
rows: someone is taking an exam or has a job interview
someone has passed an exam or had a baby

lesson.text: On someone's birthday we say **Happy Birthday!** - not ~~Congratulations~~.

exercises.explanation: We say Bless you! when someone sneezes.

exercises.prompt: Your friend is taking a driving test today. What do you say?
exercises.explanation: We say Good luck! before something difficult.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says: I passed my driving test! What do you say?
exercises.explanation: Congratulations! or Well done! after someone does something special.
On someone's birthday we say Happy Birthday, not Congratulations.

exercises.prompt: What do you say in each situation?

pairs.left: You answer the phone at work at 10.30 am.
You answer the phone at work at 3 pm.
It is 2 am on 1st January and you meet a friend.
You stand on someone's foot on a crowded bus.
It is 24th December and you meet a friend.

exercises.prompt: Some people are blocking the doorway and you want to go through. You say: ___ me!
exercises.explanation: Excuse me! is polite when you want to get past someone.

exercises.prompt: A child says Goodnight to you. You answer: Goodnight. ___ well.
exercises.explanation: Goodnight. Sleep well. is what we say at bedtime.

exercises.statement: You say Goodnight when you arrive at a party.
exercises.explanation: You say Goodnight only when you leave, or when someone goes to bed.

exercises.statement: When it is someone's birthday we say Congratulations.
exercises.explanation: When it is someone's birthday we say Happy Birthday!
Fine, thanks. And you? is the usual answer.

exercises.prompt: Say goodbye to a friend you will see again soon.
Do you say it when you meet someone, or when you leave?
A friend buys you a drink. You can say Thank you, or informally ___!
exercises.explanation: Cheers is an informal way to say thank you.
